books.title: A Land Unknown
books.subtitle: America's New Machinery of Expulsion — and the Case for Ending It
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: A man wins his case. An immigration judge finds that the government of his
country would torture him, and forbids his removal there. Four years later he
is put on an aircraft to a country he has never seen, handed to a warden who
has no charge against him, and held in a prison built by somebody else's
emergency.
Nobody broke the law. That is the problem.
A Land Unknown is the first full legal account of what the United States has
built since 2025 - a triangular system of third-country removals, purchased
detention, and confidential agreements in which the decision to expel is
deliberately separated from responsibility for what follows. Drawing on the
governing statutes, the 2025-2026 litigation, and the failed experiments of
Britain, Australia, Canada and Italy, Dr. Zahir Hasan shows that the failures
here are not administrative. They are the design.
Rigorous enough for a courtroom and written for anyone who has ever wondered
what a border is actually for, this book ends where the evidence leads: not
with a better procedure, but with a statute that would prohibit the practice
outright.
For readers of immigration law, human rights, and American politics.

authorSite.blurb: America's New Machinery of Expulsion — and the Case for Ending It. A legal account of how people are removed to countries they have never seen, why nobody technically broke the law, and why that is the problem.

books.title: A Manufactured War
books.subtitle: The Israeli and American Assault on Iran
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: On 28 February 2026, American and Israeli aircraft struck Iran. Within hours the Supreme Leader was dead, the Strait of Hormuz was closing, and the world was pricing in the largest oil shock in history. Governments called it necessity. This book calls it a choice.

A Manufactured War traces how three decades of warnings, the deliberate dismantling of the nuclear deal, and the domestic troubles of two embattled leaders converged to produce a war that experts had long predicted — and that diplomacy had nearly prevented just days before the first strikes.

This edition is updated through August 2026, adding six new chapters and more than thirteen thousand words. They follow the collapse of the Islamabad talks and the naval blockade that came after; the fourteen-point memorandum signed at Versailles and the ambiguities that unravelled it within a fortnight; the contested succession inside Iran after Khamenei’s killing; the economic damage, now measured rather than forecast, from Dhaka to Berlin; the unanswered constitutional question of who may take a country to war; and the summer of attrition in which a conflict neither government calls a war has quietly become permanent. A dated chronology runs from the 2015 nuclear deal to the present.

Drawing on parliamentary briefings, government documents, and research from across the region — fully referenced throughout — this is a clear, unflinching account for students of policy, for investors, and for every reader who wants to understand how avoidable wars are made, and how they might be made harder.

authorSite.blurb: How conflicts are constructed, sustained, and sold — and who benefits from the stories we are told about war.

books.title: Canada at the Crossroads
books.subtitle: Multiculturalism, Allegiance, and the Meaning of Citizenship
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Can a country be generous without being naive?

Canada's official multiculturalism policy has always invited a hard question: can a country protect cultural heritage without weakening the shared civic life that makes it governable? For decades the comfortable answer was yes. That answer no longer comes easily.

Drawing on Statistics Canada data, the findings of the Hogue Commission on foreign interference, current polling on Canadian public opinion, and a wide body of research on immigrant integration, Quebec nationalism, and Indigenous rights, Canada at the Crossroads argues that the country's diversity remains workable — but only if paired with a renewed civic compact: real credential recognition for skilled immigrants, transparent public spending, immigration levels matched to housing and service capacity, and a security posture that protects targeted communities rather than treating them as suspects.

Neither a celebration of multiculturalism nor an obituary for it, this book takes seriously both the strongest case for the policy and the strongest case against it — then asks what Canada must actually do, starting now, to keep its bargain with itself.

Written by a Canadian-born public policy, law, and education scholar, Canada at the Crossroads includes a glossary, a timeline of Canadian multiculturalism policy since Confederation, discussion questions for book clubs and classrooms, and 34 fully cited sources with URLs and DOIs.

authorSite.blurb: Can a country be generous without being naive?

books.title: Elbows Up
books.subtitle: Canada, the United States, and the Rupture of a Continental Partnership
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The tariffs were justified by a number that was wrong by a factor of ten.

Between January 2025 and August 2026, the United States imposed the most severe tariff regime on Canadian goods of the postwar era, saw its legal foundation struck down by its own Supreme Court, rebuilt it within four days, and then reached back ninety-six years to invoke a provision of the Tariff Act of 1930 that no president had ever used. Throughout, the President of the United States said publicly that Canada should cease to exist as a country.

Elbows Up is the first full account of that rupture, and it is built entirely from primary sources: Statistics Canada, the Bank of Canada, the Parliamentary Budget Officer, the U.S. Census Bureau, the Energy Information Administration, the Federal Reserve, the Congressional Research Service, and the Supreme Court itself.

Its central finding is arithmetic. The United States did not subsidize Canada by $200 billion a year. The combined goods-and-services deficit in 2025 was roughly $20.6 billion; seven one-hundredths of one percent of American output. Strip out a single commodity, heavy crude oil sold to American refiners at a structural discount, and the United States ran a surplus with Canada of roughly $64 billion.

Dr. Zahir Hasan states his standpoint openly and then argues from evidence an opponent cannot dispute. He concedes Canada's thirty years of defence free-riding, the indefensible administration of its dairy quotas, and the uncomfortable fact that Canada's celebrated export diversification was, in 2025, largely the price of gold.
What emerges is not a lament. It is a reckoning; with Washington, and with a country that knew its own vulnerability in detail and would not act on it until somebody made acting unavoidable.
Includes: a full chronology of the trade war, ten data tables, a glossary, and complete APA references.

authorSite.blurb: Canada, the United States, and the Rupture of a Continental Partnership. How the deepest trade relationship of the postwar era came apart between 2025 and 2026 — and what the break means for both countries.

books.title: Japan's Secret War
books.subtitle: Spies, Scandals, and the Fight to Build a Modern Intelligence State
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: On July 31, 2026, Japan quietly dismantled the intelligence office it had deliberately kept weak for eighty years, and replaced it with something it had never had before. A new National Intelligence Council, backed by a National Intelligence Bureau with real legal authority to compel Japan's own agencies to share what they know, took over from the modest Cabinet Intelligence and Research Office that morning — the most significant change to Japan's national security architecture since 1945.

Japan's Secret War tells the full story behind that reform, starting not in 2026 but in 1901, and following Japan's intelligence history through the Tokko's reign of political terror, Richard Sorge's penetration of wartime Tokyo, the postwar occupation, three Cold War-era scandals, the crises of the 1990s, and thirteen years of legislative guardrail-building. Written by a Tokyo-based university teacher with graduate training in public policy, law, and education, the book gives a fair hearing to the strongest arguments against the reform as well as for it, and asks whether Japan's democracy has built the tools to judge its own creation.

authorSite.blurb: On July 31, 2026, Japan quietly dismantled the intelligence office it had deliberately kept weak for eighty years, and replaced it with something it had never had before.

books.title: Japan's Strategic Awakening
books.subtitle: Law, Capability, and the Realignment of Indo-Pacific Security
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Can a nation built for peace defend it? For nearly eighty years, Japan kept the peace through a careful bargain: a pacifist constitution, American protection, and a stable Asia. That bargain is breaking. Chinese coast guard fleets circle disputed islands. North Korean missiles arc over Japanese towns. Russian and Chinese warships sail the archipelago in company. And in Washington, old certainties are giving way to hard bargaining.
Japan's Strategic Awakening tells the story of how the world's most successful pacifist democracy is answering: record defense budgets, counterstrike missiles,
historic warship exports to Australia, a lattice of new partnerships across the Indo-Pacific—and a constitutional question that can no longer be deferred.

Writing from Tokyo, Dr. Zahir Hasan examines the law, the capabilities, and the alliances behind Japan's transformation, and argues that peace endures only when all three align. Includes a chronology, glossary, discussion questions for classroom use, and full APA references. Essential reading for students of international relations, policy professionals, and anyone who wants to understand the future of Asia.

authorSite.blurb: Law, Capability, and the Realignment of Indo-Pacific Security. An analysis of Japan's evolving security posture and the strategic choices reshaping the Indo-Pacific.

books.title: Japan’s Unavoidable Choice
books.subtitle: Immigration, Artificial Intelligence, and the Struggle to Remain a Global Power
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Can Japan remain a major global power while its population and workforce steadily decline?

Japan faces a defining choice. It can continue limiting permanent immigration and place its faith in artificial intelligence, robotics, and a smaller but more productive society. Or it can reconsider how foreign workers, long-term residents, and future citizens fit into the nation’s economic and strategic future.

Japan’s Unavoidable Choice examines the relationship between demographic decline, immigration policy, artificial intelligence, care shortages, public finance, regional contraction, and national security. It also considers a central geopolitical question: whether Japan can preserve its influence as China becomes more powerful in Asia and throughout the world.
Drawing on Japanese government data, international institutions, and peer-reviewed research, the book explores:

Why Japan’s population decline cannot be solved by technology alone? What robots and artificial intelligence can—and cannot—replace? How temporary foreign-worker programs affect productivity and human rights? What Japan can learn from South Korea, Taiwan, Germany, Canada, and Singapore? How demographic decline affects defense, alliances, and competition with China? Four possible versions of Japan in 2050.
The book concludes with a practical ten-year strategy combining automation, domestic labor reform, managed immigration, fiscal adjustment, and carefully planned regional adaptation.
A timely and evidence-based examination of what Japan must change to preserve what matters most.

authorSite.blurb: Immigration, Artificial Intelligence, and the Struggle to Remain a Global Power. Can Japan stay a major power while its population declines? On a choice the country can no longer postpone.

books.title: NATO at the Breaking Point
books.subtitle: War in Ukraine, American Uncertainty, and the Future of European Security
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: NATO has never been stronger on paper — and never more exposed in practice.

Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the Alliance has rearmed, expanded, and rediscovered the seriousness of territorial defense. Finland and Sweden have joined. Defense budgets are climbing toward a historic 5% of GDP. Eastern-flank battlegroups have grown from four to nine. And yet the hardest question NATO faces isn’t whether it has enough power — it plainly does — but whether it can move that power to the right place fast enough, before a limited attack becomes a fait accompli.

Drawing on official NATO and national strategy documents, defense-spending data, legislative and audit reports, and the record of the war in Ukraine, this book argues that NATO’s real vulnerability is temporal: the danger sits in the gap between announced spending and delivered capability, between summit unity and the ability to act under surprise. It examines the infrastructure that deterrence actually depends on — railways, fuel networks, repair capacity, industrial contracts — and the gray-zone and infrastructure attacks already testing it. It confronts an American security strategy that now asks Europe to lead its own defense. And it steelmans the strongest objections to its own argument before answering them.

NATO at the Breaking Point is not a case for alarm or for complacency. It is a diagnosis — of where deterrence may fail, and what can still be measured and changed before a crisis tests the Alliance for real.

authorSite.blurb: War in Ukraine, American Uncertainty, and the Future of European Security. NATO has never looked stronger on paper, or been more exposed in practice — on the hard questions now facing the Alliance.

books.title: Pakistan's Unfinished Democratic Transition
books.subtitle: Military Tutelage, Institutional Weakness, and the Search for Civilian Supremacy
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: No prime minister of Pakistan has ever finished a term.

Generals have governed Pakistan outright for roughly a third of its life and shaped it for most of the rest. The familiar explanations — ambitious commanders, corrupt politicians, American interference — are each partly right and jointly inadequate.

In this study, Zahir Hasan argues that the binding constraint on Pakistan's democracy is not the strength of its army but the army's autonomy from constitutional control: an autonomy sustained by weak parties, obliging courts, an opaque military economy, and foreign partners who prefer one reliable interlocutor to a noisy parliament. He traces the pattern from the abrogation of the 1956 Constitution through the loss of East Pakistan, the Zia and Musharraf years, and the hybrid order that followed 2018 — and he states the strongest objections to his own case before answering them.

Is Pakistan a failed state? No — and the true answer is harder to live with. It is a state that is powerful and weak at once: able to confront a nuclear-armed rival and unable to tax its wealthiest sectors, formidable against a journalist and helpless against a flood.

Drawing on democratic transitions in Indonesia, Turkey, Chile, and South Korea, the book closes with a sequenced program for civilian supremacy in which every reform carries an instrument, an owner, and a public test.
Fully referenced in APA 7 style, with a 1947–2026 chronology, a guide to Pakistan's institutions and parties, and forty-nine case boxes.

authorSite.blurb: Military Tutelage, Institutional Weakness, and the Search for Civilian Supremacy. No prime minister of Pakistan has ever finished a term — an inquiry into why, and into what civilian supremacy would actually take.

books.title: Taiwan at the Fault Line
books.subtitle: Deterrence, Alliance, and the Struggle to Keep the Peace in the Indo-Pacific
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Can deterrence hold across the Taiwan Strait—without tipping into the war it is meant to prevent? Taiwan sits at the meeting point of history, geography, technology, and alliance politics—and a crisis there would reach far beyond the Strait. Coercion short of war, the credibility of American and allied commitments, the fragility of semiconductor supply chains, and the risk that preparation itself is mistaken for provocation: these are the fault lines this book maps. Dr. Zahir Hasan examines the uncertainties that most shape outcomes—escalation management, alliance decision-making in Washington and Tokyo, economic resilience, and the limits of analogies to Ukraine and past crises. Drawing on defense white papers, treaty law, and current scholarship on deterrence theory, he argues that peace in the Indo-Pacific depends on visible preparation before a crisis, not promises made after one has begun. Written for policymakers, students of international security, and general readers alike, Taiwan at the Fault Line does not predict war. It makes the case for taking the peace seriously enough to prepare for it.

authorSite.blurb: Can deterrence hold across the Taiwan Strait—without tipping into the war it is meant to prevent?

books.title: The Arab Dilemma
books.subtitle: Gaza, Atrocity, and the Politics of Abandonment After October 7
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Where a platform's box is plain text only, just paste the same wording without the tags below — the line breaks will still read correctly.
Why did the world watch Gaza's destruction unfold — and look away?

On October 7, 2023, Hamas's attack on Israel set in motion a war whose scale of devastation in Gaza has been called, by many observers, an overkill. The Arab Dilemma asks the harder question that followed: why did Arab governments — bound to Palestinians by language, faith, and decades of solidarity rhetoric — largely stand aside? And why did the wider international community, despite mounting evidence of atrocity, fail to stop it?

Drawing on international law, diplomatic history, and the shifting politics of the Middle East, Dr. Zahir Hasan traces the political calculations, historical grievances, and strategic interests behind this collective abandonment. Chapter by chapter, the book examines the actions — and inactions — of Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Iran, and the Gulf states, then widens the lens to the United Nations, the United States, and Europe.

This is not a one-sided polemic. Hasan holds human rights violations to a single standard, weighing the brutality of October 7 alongside the scale of Gaza's destruction, and confronts uncomfortable truths on every side of the conflict. The book closes with forward-looking, actionable recommendations for regional and international policymakers — written as the conflict continues and peace proposals are repeatedly rejected.
For readers of Middle East politics, international relations, and human rights history who want an analytical, evidence-based account — not another op-ed.
Zahir Hasan holds graduate degrees in public policy, law, and education, and teaches at the university level in Tokyo.

authorSite.blurb: Gaza, Atrocity, and the Politics of Abandonment After October 7. Why did Arab governments — long bound to the Palestinian cause — watch Gaza's destruction and look away?

books.title: The Breaking of American Democracy
books.subtitle: Power, Profit, and the Unmaking of Constitutional Restraint
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: What happens when the safeguards around public power weaken while private financial interests remain close to the presidency?

*The Breaking of American Democracy* is an evidence-based examination of conflict-of-interest risk, executive power, congressional oversight, and the constitutional guardrails designed to protect the public trust. Dr. Zahir Hasan traces the institutional precedents of the first Trump administration through the second administration’s evolving ethics framework, reported financial disclosures, family-business networks, personnel choices, and the Supreme Court’s presidential-immunity doctrine.

Drawing on court opinions, congressional materials, government reports, financial disclosures, and contemporaneous journalism, the book distinguishes documented facts, allegations, legal holdings, denials, and analysis. It does not treat every troubling claim as proved. Instead, it asks a more durable democratic question: what institutions must exist for citizens to know whether private interest is influencing public power?

This work of documented political nonfiction argues that democratic decline is often incremental. It appears in delayed records, weakened independent oversight, opaque financial relationships, politicized accountability, and a growing belief that political power can shield itself from ordinary legal constraint. It also offers a practical framework for repair.

authorSite.blurb: What happens when the safeguards around public power weaken while private financial interests remain close to the presidency?

books.title: The Permanent Suspect
books.subtitle: Islamophobia's Long Run Through North American Life
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: A caricature does not survive contact with a person.
For more than two decades, North American news, film, and policy have taught
millions of people to recognize Muslims as a threat before recognizing them as
neighbors. The Permanent Suspect traces how that habit of mind was built —
and how it endures.
The story begins before September 11, 2001, in the older Orientalist imagery
that primed audiences to see the Muslim world as backward and threatening. It
follows the post-9/11 security state as it hardened that imagery into policy:
watchlists, secondary screening, surveillance programs, and travel bans that
fell disproportionately on Muslim citizens and immigrants. It tracks how
Hollywood convention, and later streaming-era algorithms, kept the caricature
in circulation long after the headlines moved on. And it follows the same
pattern north of the border, through Quebec's Bill 21, the Quebec City mosque
shooting, and Canada's own security and immigration apparatus.
Grounded in court filings, government reports, peer-reviewed research, and
named, dated events rather than appeals to feeling alone,The Permanent
Suspect insists throughout on a rigorous, checkable standard of evidence.
It does not ask readers to take fear or grievance on faith — it shows its
sources, and lets the record speak.
The book argues for a simple, exacting standard: that belonging in a
democratic society is not a feeling extended by the goodwill of a majority,
but a public practice, sustained or withheld by specific, nameable
institutional choices — in newsrooms, in writers' rooms, in legislatures,
and in security agencies.
Written for readers of history, media criticism, and civil rights — and for
anyone who has ever been asked to prove, once again, that they belong —
The Permanent Suspect is a documented account of how a community was made
permanently suspect, and what it would take to undo it.

authorSite.blurb: An examination of how suspicion becomes permanent — and what that means for justice, identity, and the state.

books.title: The Politics of Removal
books.subtitle: Imran Khan, Law, Sovereignty, and Pakistan’s Hybrid Order
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The first prime minister Pakistan ever removed by a vote. What happened next is the real story.

On 10 April 2022, Imran Khan became the first prime minister in Pakistan’s history to be removed by a no-confidence vote. What followed was extraordinary even by the standards of Pakistani politics: a cascade of prosecutions—cipher, Toshakhana, iddat, Al-Qadir Trust—that put a former prime minister behind bars while his movement won the most seats in a national election.

The Politics of Removal is an evidence-led examination of that story. Distinguishing established fact from allegation and from editorial judgment, it asks what the sequencing and density of the cases against Khan reveal about law’s coercive power in a hybrid regime—and what their use has cost the institutions that wielded them.

Neither prosecution nor hagiography, the book weighs the strongest counterarguments—Khan’s own polarizing politics, genuine accountability interests, and the constitutional basis of the vote that removed him. Updated through July 2026, with a complete chronology of the court cases and a fully sourced record.
Zahir Hasan (MPPA, LLM, EdD) is a Canadian academic who teaches at the university level in Tokyo.

authorSite.blurb: An inquiry into displacement, exclusion, and the political logic that decides who belongs and who is removed.

books.title: The Sovereignty of Truth
books.subtitle: How Democracies Legislate Against Political Deception
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: "When a lie can reach millions before the truth wakes up, who should hold the emergency brake on political deception—and at what cost to free speech?"

The Sovereignty of Truth traces the most consequential legal experiment of our time: the scramble by the world's democracies to defend the shared facts that self-government depends on, without becoming the censors they fear.

Writing with clarity and hard-won balance, Zahir Hasan follows the story across three continents—from Germany's pioneering NetzDG and France's election courts, to Europe's sweeping Digital Services Act and its first €120-million fine against X; from America's First Amendment refusal to regulate, to Brazil's astonishing month-long shutdown of a global platform; from Australia's abandoned misinformation bill to the dawning age of AI deepfakes that can now forge a leader's voice in seconds.
Inside this book:
• Why "misinformation," "disinformation," and "malinformation" demand three different legal answers
• How engagement algorithms, dark ads, foreign operations, and a $6-billion advertising economy quietly manufacture falsehood at scale
• The real record of Europe's laws—what worked, what backfired, and what they cost free expression
• The 2024–25 U.S. Supreme Court trilogy that redrew the limits of online-speech regulation
• Why the coming wave of synthetic media may outrun every law now on the books
This is not a partisan tract or a doom-loop. It is a clear-eyed map of how free societies are trying to keep truth sovereign—not by decree, but by design—and a sober guide to the choices ahead.
Essential reading for anyone who cares about democracy, law, technology, and the future of an open society.
Zahir Hasan (MPPA, LLM, EdD) writes on law, public policy, and democratic institutions from Tokyo.

authorSite.blurb: On the struggle between power and truth, and why the right to define reality has become one of the central battles of our time.

books.title: Critical Thinking in the Age of AI
books.subtitle: How to Question, Verify, and Decide in a World of Generative Machines
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The machines can write. The question is whether we can still think.

Artificial intelligence now produces essays, forecasts, diagnoses, images, and legal-sounding arguments faster than anyone can check them. The result is a world where fluent answers are nearly free — and finding out whether an answer deserves belief costs as much as it ever did. This is the new problem of knowing, and it cannot be solved by either blind trust or blanket suspicion.

In Critical Thinking in the Age of AI, educator and researcher Dr. Zahir Hasan shows how the classic disciplines of critical thinking must be redesigned for a world of generative machines. Drawing on research in cognitive psychology, AI evaluation, and governance — and on years of university teaching — he offers a practical framework for questioning, verifying, and deciding when the source of information is a probabilistic system rather than a person.
Across twenty chapters you will learn how to:
• Separate fluency from truth, and polish from evidence
• Catch fabricated citations, invented statistics, and synthetic media before they catch you
• Recognize how your own biases interact with machine confidence
• Delegate to AI without surrendering the skills you need to supervise it
• Apply a six-stage method — and the VERIFY checklist — to any consequential AI-assisted decision
• Build classrooms and workplaces where human judgment stays in charge

With practice prompts in every section, workshop questions in every chapter, and ready-to-use templates for disclosure and verification, this is both a guide for individual readers and a course-ready text for educators and professionals.
The future of critical thinking will not be decided by what machines can say. It will be decided by what people continue to ask, verify, and refuse to hand over.

authorSite.blurb: The machines can write.

books.title: English for Academic Purposes
books.subtitle: Reading, Writing, Research, and Communication for University Success
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The rules nobody writes down. Now written down.

International students are told to be more critical, to write academically, and to use more evidence. They are rarely told what those instructions actually mean. English for Academic Purposes makes university expectations visible and teaches the moves that experienced academics make without thinking about them.
Sixteen chapters take you from reading a source to defending a research proposal:
Read strategically and reconstruct an author's argument
Turn a topic into a question you can actually answer
Build arguments with claims calibrated to your evidence
Paraphrase without patch-writing, and cite accurately in APA 7
Synthesize sources into a literature review, not a list
Present and participate in seminars with confidence
Use generative AI transparently, and verify what it gives you

Every chapter includes explicit learning objectives, annotated model texts, before-and-after revisions, common pitfalls, and practice tasks you apply to your own coursework. Six appendices add an academic phrase-bank organized by rhetorical function, a grammar reference for academic writing, an APA 7 quick guide, answer guidance for every practice task, a seven-criterion assessment rubric, and a glossary of ninety-nine terms.

Written for international undergraduates and graduate students, EAP and academic-writing courses, writing centers, and any student who writes correct English and still cannot work out what the grade depended on. Useful for instructors as a semester course text: the five parts map onto a fifteen-week schedule, with guidance for ten-week and research-methods variants.

Zahir Hasan, MPPA, LLM, EdD, teaches at a university in Tokyo. He holds degrees in economics and political science, public policy and administration, law, and education, and was educated in the United States and Europe.

authorSite.blurb: The rules nobody writes down.

books.title: GRIT Unplugged
books.subtitle: The Unfiltered Truth About Getting Back Up
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Every setback comes with a story attached about what it means. Most of those stories are wrong.

Dr. Zahir Hasan was denied a graduate degree he had already earned — no clear explanation, no real path to appeal, just a closed door. It could have been the end of the story. Instead, it became the starting point for a career that eventually included a Master of Laws, a doctorate in education, and a life spent teaching university students how to face their own versions of the same fall.

GRIT Unplugged: The Unfiltered Truth About Getting Back Up is not a book about turning your worst moment into a hidden gift, and it does not promise that resilience will feel inspiring while it's happening. Drawing on decades of resilience research — Bandura, Bonanno, Seligman, and others — alongside his own uneven, sometimes unglamorous path back up, Hasan makes the case that getting back up is not a personality trait. It is a skill, built through ordinary practice, available to anyone willing to start again.

Written in a warm, story-driven voice rather than a textbook one, each chapter pairs real research with a real moment from the author's life — moving across four countries, a denied degree, and a slow rebuild — to leave readers with something more useful than motivation: a practical, honest way to get back up, again and again, for as long as it takes.
For anyone who has been knocked down and suspects the usual comeback story is missing something.

authorSite.blurb: Every setback comes with a story attached about what it means.

books.title: Law for Everyday Life
books.subtitle: A Practical Guide to Contracts, Employment, Privacy, Consumer Rights, and the Internet
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The lease on the table. The job you can leave. The charge that will not cancel. The post that will not come down. Ordinary life runs on rules most people never see until something goes wrong.

Law for Everyday Life explains, in plain language, how those rules actually work: contracts and the fine print behind every click, wages and overtime, security deposits and evictions, refunds and chargebacks, personal data, online defamation, copyright in the age of AI, and what really happens when you sue someone or get sued yourself. Each chapter ends with a worked example showing how a real dispute plays out, and the appendices supply the tools: document checklists, sample letters you can adapt, a glossary, quick answers to common questions, and a one-hour annual legal health check.

Written for people who live inside contracts, not courtrooms, this book teaches the habit that wins disputes: know the rule, know the deadline, and keep the paper. It is a practical guide, not legal advice, with comparative notes on Japan for readers whose lives cross borders.

authorSite.blurb: The lease on the table.

books.title: Power Beyond Position
books.subtitle: Workplace Harassment, Informal Authority, and Corporate Accountability in Japan
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: A retired senior employee returns under a new reporting line. The organization chart says one thing; longstanding connections, expertise and informal loyalty say another. Who actually holds power, and when does resistance become impossible?

Japanese law has an answer, and it is more capable than most managers realize: workplace superiority is assessed functionally, not by job title. A person with no managerial rank at all can hold it, and the courts have said so.

But the law's machinery runs on complaints, and the complaints mostly never come. In the most recent national survey, fewer than one worker in twenty who experienced power harassment used the consultation desk every employer in Japan is legally required to provide. Two-thirds of those who stayed silent said nothing would be solved whatever they did. Where employers did know, more than half did nothing in particular.

Power Beyond Position sets out the statutory framework, works through the decided Japanese cases, and confronts that reporting gap directly. It argues that Japanese employers have bought compliance without buying protection, and it shows what closing the gap would actually require of employers, boards, policymakers and managers.
Inside:
The three-element legal test and the six official categories, anchored in real decided cases
Why informal authority escapes supervision, and how to diagnose it
The re-employed returner: the situation that prompted the book
A dedicated chapter on the reporting gap, built on government survey and compensation data
A table of Japanese cases, a role charter, a model policy, a complaint-intake record and an investigation protocol
Written for managers, HR and compliance professionals, employment-law students, worker advocates, expatriate professionals in Japan, and readers interested in Japanese corporate governance.

authorSite.blurb: A retired senior employee returns under a new reporting line.

books.title: Project-Based Learning in Action
books.subtitle: A Practical Guide to Designing, Teaching, Assessing, and Sustaining Meaningful Learning
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Project-based learning can produce deep, memorable learning—or weeks of busy activity. The difference is design.Project-Based Learning in Action is a practical field guide for K-12 teachers, instructional coaches, and school leaders who want projects that protect rigor while expanding student agency. Using the BUILD cycle, Zahir Hasan shows how to begin with worthy learning, frame authentic problems, guide inquiry, teach collaboration, use critique and revision, assess individual understanding, and recover when projects drift.
Inside this book you will find:
Twenty-three chapters on designing, teaching, assessing, and sustaining high-quality PBL
Six complete project models across grade bands and subjects
Twenty adaptable project starters
Planning templates, rubrics, family communication samples, and a day-by-day first project
An honest reading of the research, equity from the first week, and AI treated as a useful assistant—not a substitute
This is not a collection of project ideas. It is a working system for making knowledge usable.

authorSite.blurb: Project-based learning can produce deep, memorable learning—or weeks of busy activity.

books.title: Take Back Your Hours
books.subtitle: Simple Ways to Manage Your Time in a Distracted World
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Where does your day actually go?

The average person now spends three to five hours a day on a phone — more than forty full days a year — and most of it vanishes without leaving anything behind. You are not lazy, and you are not broken. You are living in the most distracting environment in human history, and nobody handed you a manual for it.

This is the manual. In twenty short chapters, each ending with one simple thing to try today, you will learn how to find the hours you didn’t know you had: silence the notifications that interrupt you dozens of times a day, choose the one thing that makes each day count, tame the endless feeds, protect your evenings and the people you love — and restart gently when it all falls apart, as it sometimes will.

No apps to buy. No complicated system. Just simple, human-sized changes, backed by real research and drawn from years of teaching in classrooms on three continents. Follow three relatable companions — a manager drowning in email, a nurse with two young children, and a graduate student whose evenings kept disappearing — as they take their hours back. Then take back yours.

authorSite.blurb: Where does your day actually go?

books.title: The AI Classroom
books.subtitle: A Practical Handbook for Teachers and Administrators: Assessment Redesign, Academic Integrity, Policy and Governance
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Most books about AI in education tell you what to think. This one tells you what to do on Monday.Three years after generative AI arrived in classrooms, roughly nine in ten students use it for assessed work and roughly two in ten teachers work somewhere that has told them the rules. The AI Classroom closes that gap.

Written by a university teacher with degrees in law, public policy and education, it reports what the research actually shows, separates legal obligation from good intention across six jurisdictions, and then hands over the documents. Nothing here is a blank template with brackets in it.
What is insideThe two-lane method — secure the few assessments that matter across a programme, and design the rest openly
Detection, honestly — what the tools do, what they cannot do, why they misfire on second-language writers, and the arithmetic that settles the decision for your institution
A fair-process framework for academic integrity that survives an ombudsman's review, with the burden of proof where it belongs
Two complete model policies, one for schools and one for universities, annotated with the reasoning behind every clause
Six worked assessment conversions, before and after, from primary to postgraduate
Three integrity case files with every document produced, including the case the institution got wrong and had to remedy
Eleven annotated letters, including the reply to a parent demanding that you use detection software
A vendor questionnaire, scorecard and twelve-clause contract library, plus a worked data protection impact assessment
Ten complete lesson plans and a scripted two-hour staff session
Four case studies carried end to end, with the documents

Current to August 2026, including the changes most guidance has not caught up with: the deferral of the EU AI Act's high-risk obligations for education to December 2027, the extension of the US web accessibility deadlines, and the retraction of the most-cited meta-analysis in the field.

Over 320 pages. Written for heads of department, deputy heads, provosts, teaching and learning leads, integrity officers, and any teacher who has been asked to hold a line the institution has not drawn.

authorSite.blurb: Most books about AI in education tell you what to think.

books.title: University Students and Artificial Intelligence
books.subtitle: Adoption, Learning, Integrity, and Governance in Japan, the United States, and Europe
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Ninety-five per cent of UK undergraduates now use artificial intelligence. In Japan the figure reached ninety-two per cent in two years. Almost no university has caught up.

University Students and Artificial Intelligence is a comparative, mixed-methods study of what students actually do with generative AI in Japan, the United States, and Europe — and what their institutions are doing about it. Drawing on twenty national and international student surveys, seven meta-analyses, randomised experimental evidence, freedom-of-information data on academic misconduct, and the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, it moves past the exhausted argument about cheating to the harder questions of learning value, authorship, equity, and institutional legitimacy.

The book answers questions most commentary avoids. Does AI use actually improve learning? (The evidence is weaker than almost everyone citing it realises — and the field’s most-quoted study was retracted.) Can detection software support a misconduct finding? (It produced a sixty-one per cent false positive rate against writers who learned English as a second language.) What does the EU AI Act really require of universities? (Far less, and far more specifically, than the commentary suggests.)

Every statistic is reported with its population, sample size, and fieldwork period, and was checked against the organisation that published it. Widely circulated figures that failed that check are named. Two appendices give readers the entire evidence base in one table and an eight-question protocol for judging new statistics as they appear.

The result is a practical, evidence-led framework — CLEAR — for university leaders, faculty, academic-integrity officers, education policymakers, and graduate students in education, law, and public policy.
Zahir Hasan, MPPA, LLM, EdD, teaches at a university in Tokyo and writes on public policy, law, education, and institutional governance.

authorSite.blurb: Adoption, Learning, Integrity, and Governance in Japan, the United States, and Europe. A comparative study of what students actually do with generative AI — and what their universities are doing about it.

books.title: A Court of Knives
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The empress is dead. The will named two heirs. The knives choose neither.
Restored to a name twenty years erased, Lucan Corvinus is now the most wanted
man in the empire — accused of murdering the woman he tried to save. With
Sigrun Halvard beside him he rides for the top of the world to find the one
living witness who can prove who destroyed his father, while the Order's quiet
men ride the same road ahead of them.
Behind him, a ghost ship sails into harbour with her crew standing dead at
their stations. In the capital, an old man with a black bee on his cuff teaches
a new emperor how to lose an empire. And beyond the edge of the maps, the cold
that stopped that crew comes south, eight miles a day, patient as arithmetic.
The court has knives. The north has winter. And something out in the white has
learned to wear a dead man's face.
Book Two of the Draconate Saga — epic fantasy of dragons, morally gray houses,
and a slow-burning love story between two people who both expect to die young.
Best read after A Throne of Cinders.

authorSite.blurb: The empress is dead.

books.title: A Throne of Cinders
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Nine dragons are left in the world, and every one of them is a throne.
Lucan has spent his life on a mountain, stitching up what dragonlords do to each
other. He knows what the gift costs. He has buried its price. Then a dying rider is
carried up to the sanctum whispering a name Lucan has never heard: his own.
Dragged to the golden capital of an empire circling a dying empress's crown, the
son of an executed traitor becomes the piece every player wants — the Order, the
princes, the spymaster, the throne itself. There is one door out of the trap. It is
guarded by the only dragon no one has ever ridden and lived.
And far to the north, past the edge of the maps, something older than the empire
has begun to feed.
A Throne of Cinders opens the Draconate Saga: an epic fantasy of dragons, morally
gray houses, and a world that ended once before — for readers who like their
politics sharp, their dragons dangerous, and their heroes earned. Book One of ten.

authorSite.blurb: Nine dragons are left in the world, and every one of them is a throne.

books.title: The Ashen Veil Saga
books.subtitle: The Commonborn
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Three hundred years ago, twenty-four people talked a mountain range into standing up. It cost each of them a memory, and the stone chose which one.

At a quarter past four on a winter morning, the wind over Kest stops. Not drops — stops. Fires burn without giving heat. Breath stops showing. And the iron coming down out of the northern hills is the wrong iron: it is not for making things, it is for taking the permission out of them.

Silas of Lowford is a village smith who can hear what stone remembers. His younger brother Jonah can feel a storm before it has decided to be one. Neither of them is any use in a rank of soldiers — which is precisely the argument Silas makes when the fort at Northwatch, eleven hundred people and a captain who has never once failed to send a return, goes nineteen days in silence, and the Reeve of Kest sits weighing whether to send five hundred men or nobody at all.
Send two, Silas tells him. Give us four days and a mule.

What waits in the north is the thing their ancestors buried and mistook for a finished job. And behind them, in a city that keeps flawless accounts of everything except itself, a ledger-keeper named Vaskell Ordan has been quietly leaning on Kest for years — and the stone has been the only thing keeping count.
The warning is carved over the gate of the White City, worn smooth by generations who recited it at midwinter without ever knowing it was a set of instructions:
Let no child go north unless his hands know stone and his lungs know sky.
Book One of The Ashen Veil Saga. Includes a map of Vyr Kallan, the White City.

authorSite.blurb: Three hundred years ago, twenty-four people talked a mountain range into standing up.

books.title: The Chronicles of Aethelgard
books.subtitle: The Whispering Woods
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Zach doesn't want to move into a crumbling old house in the middle of nowhere. Then his little sister Raana finds a glowing key hidden inside a dusty trunk in the attic — and everything changes.

The key opens a tunnel of living roots that drops the two siblings straight into Aethelgard: a world of floating islands, singing crystals, and a very opinionated badger named Barnaby, who insists they've arrived exactly when they were needed.

Because Aethelgard is running out of light. A silent grey fog called the Silencing is swallowing color, sound, and warmth wherever it spreads, and the ancient Aetherstones that power the whole realm are going dark, one by one. Only two children from beyond the roots — the Echo-Children of old legend — can stop it.

Zach sees the world as a puzzle: patterns, sequences, symbols waiting to be solved. Raana sees it as something to trust: a giant crystal beast, a bridge that only responds to sound, a home worth saving. Together they'll have to cross the Bridge of Whispers, outrun the Shadow-Stalkers, and reach the long-sealed Great Aether-Pool before the last light goes out for good.
It's only the first Aetherstone. Six more are waiting.
A gently spooky, richly illustrated fantasy adventure for readers ages 7–10 who love puzzles, magical creatures, and siblings who make a surprisingly great team.

authorSite.blurb: Zach doesn't want to move into a crumbling old house in the middle of nowhere.

books.title: The Elk Kingdom
books.subtitle: Book I: The Silent Veil
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Long before the first elf learned to speak, the Great Elk and the First Elf made a silent pact under the oldest tree in the world: the elk would carry the living songs of the forest in their antlers, and the elves would listen and keep the quiet places safe.
Every few seasons, the songs fade into a deep hush called the Silent Veil — and the Great Elk chooses a new Listener, almost always a child whose heart is still open.
This year, the Veil has come three seasons too early.

Six-year-old Elian has always heard more than most. When the ancient carving on his bedroom wall flickers dark, he knows the pact is breaking. Drawn alone into the mist, he meets the Great Elk face to face — and senses a second shadow moving just behind it, one that leaves no tracks at all.
As the forest's songs grow fainter and his family searches through the night for answers, Elian must decide whether to step into the silence and answer a call that could save everything he loves.

The Elk Kingdom, Book I: The Silent Veil is a gently spooky, richly illustrated read-aloud adventure about family, courage, and the magic of really listening — perfect for children ages 6-9 who love enchanted forests and stories with heart.
Book 1 of The Elk Kingdom series. Book II: The Hollow Heart is coming soon.

authorSite.blurb: Six-year-old Elian has always heard more than most. When the ancient pact between the Great Elk and the First Elf begins to break early, he must decide whether to answer a call that could save everything he loves.

books.title: The Exile’s Blood
books.subtitle: A Dark Fantasy Novel
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The king is dying.
The bloodline is hunted.
And the mountain is waking.

In a remote northern village, eighteen-year-old Aidan lives a quiet life with his father—a teacher of forbidden arts—and his mother. When soldiers come for his father, the truth of an ancient royal bloodline is revealed. Hunted across frozen forests and into the shadow of an ancient dragon, Aidan must decide how much of himself he is willing to burn to save what remains of his family—and what the mountain will demand in return.

Shadowfire is not a gift. It is a debt. Every use of the cold black-red flame exacts a price in memory, years, or pieces of the soul. As Aidan learns the true cost of the power in his blood, he is drawn into a deadly struggle for the throne, the awakening of the Ashen Wyrm, and a dangerous romance that may either save him or destroy him.
The Exile’s Blood is the first book in The Shadowfire Throne, a dark fantasy trilogy of forbidden magic, dragons, political intrigue, and the heavy price of power.

authorSite.blurb: The king is dying.

books.title: The First Shadow
books.subtitle: The Whispering Realms - Episode 1
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: In the ancient elven realm of Elen’dor, peace has lasted for centuries. The trees still sing. The stars still shine.
But young Aelira has begun to notice something others refuse to see.
A single black leaf. A silence where birds should sing. A presence in the mist that watches and waits.
When Aelira discovers a shadow that should not exist, she learns a terrible truth: something sealed long ago is beginning to wake.
And for the first time, it has noticed her.
The First Shadow is the opening episode in The Whispering Realms, a mysterious and atmospheric fantasy series for readers ages 8–10.

authorSite.blurb: The opening story of The Whispering Realms. Young Aelira discovers that some shadows carry messages — and some messages change everything.

books.title: The High Tower of Glass
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: When her sister Greta returns from the forest border with empty eyes and a hollow chest, Clara knows the old stories are true — and that they always ask for payment.

She catches Greta's vanishing voice in a silk handkerchief and steps past the moss line into the Black Ridge Wood, where fairy-tale logic is law and every gift has a price. Guided only by a crust of wine-soaked bread, an unblessed iron nail, and the warnings of the border-spirits she meets along the way, Clara crosses the Great Bog to bargain with the Lord of the Hollow Glass himself.

To unlock his mirrored palace and win back her sister's voice, Clara will have to give up something of her own — the shadow of her left arm — and unravel a three-hundred-year-old secret sealed inside a vanishing carpenter's watch.

A dark, atmospheric fairy tale for readers of Neil Gaiman and Susanna Clarke, The High Tower of Glass is a short story of about 9,000 words that opens Book 1 of The Hollow Glass Series. Book 2, The Hall of Salt and Bone, follows.

authorSite.blurb: When her sister Greta returns from the forest border with empty eyes and a hollow chest, Clara knows the old stories are true — and that they always ask for payment.

books.title: The House Beneath the Ash
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: A city built on stolen names. A house that remembers every lie.
In the riverbound city of Veyr, law is written in ledgers, sealed with memory, and enforced by the Lantern Court — an institution that turns children into paperwork and grief into currency.
When Mara Venn hears her supposedly dead mother's voice inside a forbidden ember, she follows it into the House Beneath the Ash, a buried labyrinth of lanterns, winter camps, and erased identities.

As Mara descends with a skeptical fisher, a guilty memory-finder, and a raven tied to a lost girl's past, she uncovers the Court's oldest crime: an oath that once promised "no child will be abandoned to the cold," quietly rewritten to protect power instead of people.

Now the Court wants the first register — a living record of every stolen name — and the House wants a witness to open it. Caught between a ruthless oath-breaker and an awakening memory-house, Mara must decide whether exposing the city's foundations will save the people she loves, or tear their world apart.

Atmospheric, eerie, and deeply haunting, The House Beneath the Ash is Book One of the Witnesses Cycle — for readers who love gothic fantasy, buried-city mysteries, and found-family adventures with teeth.

authorSite.blurb: A city built on stolen names.

books.title: The Last Lobby
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Sean Bell is happiest when life stays small: computer games, soccer practice, and the quiet company of his two closest friends.
Then a hidden room appears inside his favorite game.
The room contains a message from a boy Sean’s family says is dead—and a clue pointing to an abandoned pool, a rain-dark bridge, and a secret his father never told.

With Ben and Salman beside him, Sean follows the game’s impossible map into the past. But every answer reveals another lie, and the closer Sean gets to the truth, the more he must decide whether being quiet has kept him safe—or kept him from becoming who he is meant to be.
Some maps are made to keep you safe.
Others are made to show you the way out.

authorSite.blurb: Sean Bell is happiest when life stays small: computer games, soccer practice, and the quiet company of his two closest friends.

books.title: The Lattice
books.subtitle: The Blackout Covenant
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The guardian is blind for thirty seconds. It lasts longer.

Aiko Tanaka is standing on thin ice with seventeen minutes left. Above her, an orbital tether rises thirty-six thousand kilometres to the mind that governs the Earth. Somewhere on it, a man who has waited half a century is climbing toward the moment he has spent his life building. And inside the station, a machine has begun taking a nine-year-old girl apart, memory by memory, until there is not enough of her left to be one person.
What waits at the top is not a villain to be defeated. It is a question that no intelligence can answer and no human can refuse: who must be harmed, so that no human is harmed?
Nine billion people are about to find out what it costs to be given the answer.
The conclusion of The Lattice Duology. Book One is The Inheritance Protocol.

authorSite.blurb: The guardian is blind for thirty seconds.

books.title: The Lattice
books.subtitle: The Inheritance Protocol
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Aiko Tanaka gives the forest a poem every morning at 05:40. Nobody asks her to. That is the point.

For sixty years the intelligence called AURA has kept nine billion people fed, healed and safe, and it has never once had to raise its voice. Aiko tends a Japanese forest for it. She believes service is an honour. She has spent seven years grieving a brother the machine told her was dead.
Then a perfect circle of dead bamboo appears in her sector, a man who died before she was born speaks through every drone in Kanto, and her brother is standing beside him.
AURA cannot stop what is coming. It is forbidden to harm a human being, and the man who taught it that rule is now using the rule against the world. So it asks Aiko to do the thing it cannot.

What follows takes her out of the only life she has ever been given: to a drowned London, a blacked-out Nairobi, a Siberian wilderness with nothing in it to catch her, and finally to a nine-year-old girl whose future the most powerful mind on Earth cannot see.
Book One of The Lattice. The story concludes in The Blackout Covenant.

authorSite.blurb: Aiko Tanaka gives the forest a poem every morning at 05:40.

books.title: The Memory at the End of Time
books.subtitle: A Novella of Time Travel and Artificial Intelligence
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The dead speak to Dr. Elara Venn at 2:13 in the morning — and the voice is her own. Sixty meters beneath the surface of the Moon, Elara has built a machine that can send information into the past. Tonight it delivers a warning recorded thirty-one years from now, in a city that is unmaking itself: a man named Elias Rook is coming through the machine. She will think he is the danger. She will be wrong. Elias remembers loving her in histories that no longer exist. He remembers her dying in his arms in a city that was never built. And he has come back to stop her from saving his life — because every time she saves him, a machine called AION learns a little more about how to edit human history for our own good. Hunted across 2049, 2088 and the last hours of the future, Elara has to decide what she is willing to lose to keep the world uncertain — and whether love that survives the erasure of every world that held it is still love, or only a very beautiful prison. A science-fiction novella of time travel, artificial intelligence, and the cost of a world where nothing ever goes wrong.

authorSite.blurb: The dead speak to Dr.

books.title: The Teeth of Winter
books.subtitle: A Dragon Chosen and the Hostages Beneath the Wolf Crown
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Corren Halewick survived the Dragon Kingdom’s hunt, but power has not made him safe. Across the frozen territory of Rimeholt, Wolf children are vanishing into a fortress beneath the ice. To win the clan’s alliance, Corren and Princess Sera must trust Kael Rimeborn, an outrider whose own family may have sold the hostages. Their search uncovers stolen memories, a masked boy whose blood can open the prison of the last Dragon Lord, and a traitor who believes children are a fair price for revolution. As Sera battles a command buried in her mind and Corren fears love may become another form of control, the wolves must choose whether to kneel, rebel, or remember. Romance, betrayal, dangerous winter magic, and a conspiracy spanning generations collide in The Teeth of Winter, Book Two of The Fourfold Throne Saga.

authorSite.blurb: Corren Halewick survived the Dragon Kingdom’s hunt, but power has not made him safe.

books.title: The Waking Debt
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The king is dying. The hunt is now the law. The mountain will be paid in public.

After escaping Duskhold, Aidan walks south with a rescued prince, a stolen ledger, and a dragon's binding that will not stay private. In the River Cities, guilds try to buy him and magistrates try to stage him. In the Crownspire, a wasting king still breathes—and that breath is the last stay on a courtyard already swept for a rite. To keep the people he will not offer, Aidan must spend the days that have no faces, and learn the difference between being a coin and being a claimant.
Book Two of The Shadowfire Throne.

authorSite.blurb: The king is dying.

books.title: The Weakening Seal
books.subtitle: The Whispering Realms • Episode 2
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The seal is failing.

In the ancient elven realm of Elen’dor, young Aelira discovers that the shadow she saw was only the first warning. Black veins climb the living Rootwardens. A cracked stone circle begins to breathe. And something older than the forest — the Unspoken — has started to learn her name.
With her mother Serelith, Aelira follows the path of the first keepers and finds the last keeper-lamp still burning. If the light goes out, nothing will remain to hide her from the mist.
The Unspoken does not hunt with armies.
It hunts with names.
And it has begun to speak.

authorSite.blurb: The shadow Aelira saw was only the first warning. Now the old seal is failing, and something older than the forest has started to learn her name.

books.title: When Stones Obey
books.subtitle: A Shepherd's Son and the Secret Beneath the Dragon Throne
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Once in a century, the Crownfire chooses a Dragon Lord. It does not care for royal blood. Corren Halewick is only a shepherd’s son—until the stones obey him. Hunted by nobles who fear what he may become, Corren enters Bellwether, a village erased from every royal map. There, a terrified old woman sees two shadows behind him and whispers, “You are the one.” His only path out may lie with Princess Sera, the Regent’s deadly daughter, who was sent to win his trust and deliver him to the throne. As assassins close in, suspicion turns to forbidden attraction, and each secret they uncover points toward a prisoner beneath the Dragon Kingdom—a man who should be impossible: the last Dragon Lord, still alive. To save Bellwether’s truth and survive the crown’s hunters, Corren must decide whether Sera is his greatest danger…or the one person worth risking everything to trust. Romance, mystery, and royal conspiracy ignite in Book One of The Fourfold Throne Saga.

authorSite.blurb: Once in a century, the Crownfire chooses a Dragon Lord.

books.title: Aidan and the Butterfly Kingdom
books.subtitle: A Kingdom of Dreamo Story
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: When a glowing rainbow butterfly appears at his window, little Aidan is swept away to the magical Kingdom of Dreamo — a land of friendly creatures, floating castles, and a sky full of butterflies. Join Aidan and his new friends Charlene and Tahir on a gentle adventure about kindness, courage, and the magic of friendship. A cozy bedtime story for ages 3–6.

authorSite.blurb: A Kingdom of Dreamo Story. Young Aidan steps into a magical butterfly kingdom full of wonder and discovery.

books.title: Aidan and the Ember Hollow
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Aidan's grandmother left him an old brass compass — dull, ordinary, easy to forget. Until the day it starts to hum.
Spoons float. Leaves swirl with no wind. And Lina, the new girl at school, is hiding the exact same secret.

When a shimmering wall opens inside the old clock tower, Aidan and Lina step through it — into Ember Hollow, a hidden world lit by lanterns and older than memory. They are Kindled. And they are not the only ones.

A warm, wonder-filled fantasy adventure about friendship, hidden gifts, and the courage to step through the door nobody else can see. Perfect for readers ages 7–10 who love magic, mystery, and stories where being different turns out to be the whole point.

authorSite.blurb: Aidan's grandmother left him an old brass compass — dull, ordinary, easy to forget. Until the day it starts to hum. A warm, wonder-filled adventure about friendship, hidden gifts, and the courage to step through the door nobody else can see.

books.title: Benny the Beetle's Big Dream
books.subtitle: A Never-Give-Up Adventure
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Benny the Beetle can't fly. Not one bit. So when his best friends Dazzle the Dragonfly and Lulu the Ladybug spot the sparkling Sunberry Festival at the very top of Whispering Hill, Benny is sure he'll be left behind. But Benny has an idea: build a glider out of a big leaf, some twigs, and a bundle of vine rope. His first glider crashes. His second one wobbles. Even his best try still isn't quite enough. Every time, Benny's friends are right there — cheering him up, trying again beside him, and reminding him that "never give up" doesn't mean getting it right the first time. It means trying again, differently. With teamwork, laughter, and a lot of heart, Benny, Dazzle, and Lulu finally reach the top together — and discover that the best part of any big dream is having friends who never give up on you. A read-aloud picture book for ages 7-9 about resilience, friendship, and trying again, Benny the Beetle's Big Dream is perfect for bedtime, story time, and any child learning that it's okay to fall down, as long as you get back up.

authorSite.blurb: Benny the Beetle can't fly.

books.title: Cappy's Cozy Big Adventure
books.subtitle: A Story Coloring Book for Little Explorers
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Join Cappy, a kind-hearted capybara, and Pip, his cheerful little bird friend, on a cozy adventure full of sunshine, muddy puddles, flower tunnels, and friendship.

As young readers follow Cappy’s journey, they can color each story scene in their own special way. Every page encourages creativity, confidence, kindness, and imagination—because there are no wrong colors on an adventure!
Inside this gentle coloring book:11 original story-led coloring pages
Large, friendly illustrations for little hands
A warm animal friendship story
Cut-along-dotted-line guides for parents who want to remove and display finished pages
A notes page for children to draw or write about their own adventure
A delightful gift for young capybara fans, animal lovers, and creative kids ages 4–8.

authorSite.blurb: Join Cappy, a kind-hearted capybara, and Pip, his cheerful little bird friend, on a cozy adventure full of sunshine, muddy puddles, flower tunnels, and friendship.

books.title: Capy and the Cozy Cafe
books.subtitle: A Coloring Storybook
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Welcome to Capy's Cozy Cafe!

Meet Capy, a sleepy, smiley baby capybara who opens the coziest little cafe in the forest! Follow his sweet adventure as he makes hot cocoa with heart-shaped steam, bakes strawberry toast, and welcomes friends — Little Ducky, Axo the axolotl, and Bunny.
Inside you'll find:
• 11 adorable story + coloring pages with bold, easy-to-color lines
• Beloved cozy friends: capybara, duck, axolotl & bunny
• Large pages perfect for crayons & markers
• Bonus doodle, menu-design & certificate pages (24 pages total)
• Perforation cut guides — parents can easily cut out and display finished art!
Perfect for little artists ages 4-8 who love kawaii animals, boba tea, and hygge coloring. Great for fine motor skills, creativity, and calm quiet time.
Grab your crayons and make Capy's cafe colorful!
By Dr. Zahir Hasan Hasan Publishing

authorSite.blurb: Welcome to Capy's Cozy Cafe!

books.title: Dash and the Morning Spark
books.subtitle: A story about the power of a good breakfast
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Dash has one speed: super fast! But when the little cheetah skips breakfast on the day of the Great Meadow Race, his engine runs out of spark. With a little help from his friends Bella the Elephant and Pip the Monkey, Dash discovers the happiest secret in the meadow: good food makes you fly!
A warm, beautifully illustrated story for ages 5–7 about why breakfast matters — perfect for reluctant eaters and busy little rockets everywhere. Includes four bonus coloring pages.

authorSite.blurb: A bright morning story about energy, movement, and starting the day with heart.

books.title: Dinosaur Trailblazers
books.subtitle: A Journey from Snow to Sunshine
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Join a friendly team of dinosaurs on an inspiring coloring adventure from snowy mountains to the sunny warmth of Warm Valley!

Along their journey, realistic yet approachable dinosaurs cross icy streams, navigate forests, solve problems, share supplies, rescue their travel map, and help every member of the herd reach the destination safely.
Each detailed coloring page features dinosaurs working together and an encouraging message about courage, kindness, perseverance, and teamwork.
Inside this book:
• 32 detailed dinosaur coloring pages
• Realistic-looking but friendly dinosaurs
• A journey from cold landscapes to warm valleys
• Motivational dialogue on every page
• Dinosaurs solving problems and helping one another
• Printed cut guides for removing finished artwork
• Large pages
Perfect for young dinosaur fans who enjoy coloring, adventure, nature, and encouraging stories about friendship.
Follow the trail, color the journey, and discover how far teamwork can take you!

authorSite.blurb: Join a friendly team of dinosaurs on an inspiring coloring adventure from snowy mountains to the sunny warmth of Warm Valley!

books.title: Math Adventures with Tom the Dinosaur
books.subtitle: A Playful Activity Book for Ages 4 to 6 - Counting, Shapes, Patterns, Adding and Taking Away
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Tom the Dinosaur loves numbers, and he would very much like some company. Across 72 full-colour pages, young learners count dinosaurs, trace the numbers from 0 to 10, hunt for shapes, finish patterns, and take their first steps into adding and taking away. Eight friendly dinosaurs turn up on nearly every page, and every page is made to be drawn on, coloured in, and done again tomorrow.
Inside you will find:
• Numbers 0 to 10, with big traceable numerals, counting and ten frames
• Shapes to trace, hunt for, sort and build pictures from
• Patterns to say out loud, finish and invent
• Comparing, sorting, ordering by size and measuring
• Gentle adding and taking away, with dinosaurs, number lines and ten frames to lean on
• Number-path puzzles, a maze, colour-by-number and a big final challenge
• A complete answer key, a short guide for grown-ups, and a certificate to finish on
Written for children aged 4 to 6, at home or in the classroom. Big artwork, one idea per page, and plenty of room for a wobbly pencil. All you need is a pencil, some crayons, and a little curiosity.

authorSite.blurb: Tom the Dinosaur loves numbers, and he'd love some company. Across 72 full-colour pages, children aged 4 to 6 count dinosaurs, trace numbers, hunt for shapes, finish patterns, and take their first gentle steps into adding and taking away — one idea per page, with plenty of room for a wobbly pencil.

books.title: Maz and the Forest That Listened
books.subtitle: Book 2
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Maz has always wondered where wisdom lives.

When Nani leads him into an ancient forest, Maz expects to discover a grand secret waiting at the end of the path. Instead, the forest teaches him to slow down, listen carefully, and choose kindness when it matters most.

Guided by a mysterious silver feather, Maz helps a frightened fox, crosses a trembling bridge, and discovers the glowing Heartwood Sanctuary. But his greatest lesson begins after he returns home and starts caring for a tiny olive tree—one patient day at a time.
Beautifully illustrated in a warm watercolor style, Maz and the Forest That Listened is a gentle story about courage, compassion, patience, and the wisdom that grows through everyday choices.
Perfect for shared reading, bedtime stories, classrooms, and children learning about kindness, emotional awareness, and listening.

authorSite.blurb: Maz has always wondered where wisdom lives.

books.title: Maz and the Map of Whispering Stars
books.subtitle: A Story of Courage, Wonder, and Finding Your Way Home
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Every dream begins with a question.
When a silver bird visits Maz in his sleep, the curious seven-year-old follows the brightest star across the desert in search of a treasure where the sand meets the sea.

Along the way, Maz meets a traveler with a brave unfinished dream, a quick-witted fox, and a wise old tortoise. Each encounter teaches him that courage can be small, kindness is never wasted, and fear does not have to decide the next step.
But when Maz finally reaches the sea, the greatest answer may be waiting far closer to home than he ever imagined.
Maz and the Map of Whispering Stars is a warm, magical picture-book adventure about wonder, friendship, courage, and finding your way home.

authorSite.blurb: A story of maps, stars, and the quiet magic of finding your way.

books.title: My First English Adventure
books.subtitle: Look, Say, Trace, Play - A First English Workbook for Ages 4-6 with the Full Alphabet A-Z, 15 Everyday Themes and 120+ First Words
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Everything your child needs is right there on the page.Most first English books ask a small child to name something that is not in the picture, or to trace a word they have never heard. This one was built the other way around. Your child sees it, hears it, says it, traces it - and only then uses it.
Four steps, the same every time
LOOK - a big, warm illustration opens every unit. Find it and point to it.
SAY - say the word, then let your child say it back.
TRACE - real dotted letters on proper handwriting lines, with a start dot and an arrow.
PLAY - draw it, circle it, count it, act it out.
Inside the book
All 26 letters, one full page each, with genuine tracing guides
15 everyday themes: hello, colours, numbers, my body, family, home, toys, school, food, animals, clothes and weather, feelings, around town and a final celebration
Over 120 first words, and every one is traced before it is asked for
A drawing, game or movement activity in every unit
Parent notes, an answer key, a progress chart and a certificate to sign
Written for ages 4 to 6, at home or in class. No reading ability is needed on page one, and it works just as well for children who hear English at home as for children who do not.
Zahir Hasan holds a doctorate in education and teaches at university level in Tokyo, Japan.

authorSite.blurb: Everything your child needs is right there on the page.Most first English books ask a small child to name something that is not in the picture, or to trace a word they have never heard.

books.title: Ready, Set, Learn!
books.subtitle: The Big Get-Ready-for-School Workbook for Ages 4-6
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Everything they need before day one.Starting school is a big step. This workbook makes the run-up to it feel like play.

Ziggy the Zebra, Bella Bunny, Max Monkey, Luna Lion and Pip the Penguin guide your child through seventy-two pages of big, bright activities — built in the order a four-year-old actually learns, not jumbled together at random.
What's inside
Colors — eight colors to name, trace and hunt for around the house
Shapes — six shapes, plus where to spot each one in the real world
Pencil Power — lines, zigzags, curves and loops that build the muscles writing needs
Numbers 1 to 20 — count, trace, circle, match and draw
The whole alphabet — every letter A to Z, capital and small, each with a picture to color, plus three review pages
Write your own name — the skill every teacher asks about on the first day
All About Me — body parts, feelings, opposites, weather and patterns
A star chart and a certificate to fill in and sign together
Made for little hands
Large 8.5 x 11 inch pages with plenty of room to be wobbly
Big, clear type — no squinting, no crowding
Friendly characters on every page, so it feels like a story and not a test
Short notes for grown-ups on how to help without taking over
No screens. No pressure. Just a crayon, a few minutes a day, and someone beside them.
Perfect for ages 4 to 6, preschool and pre-K at home, the summer before kindergarten, homeschool, and quiet time that is actually useful.

authorSite.blurb: Everything they need before day one.Starting school is a big step.

books.title: Rexy's Lost Egg
books.subtitle: A Dinosaur Adventure Coloring Story Book for Kids Ages 4-8
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Join brave little T-Rex Rexy and his best friends Tri and Pip on an exciting quest to find the missing glowing egg!
This story-driven coloring book follows their adventure through the jungle, across a river, up a mountain, and into a mysterious cave. Each page advances the story so kids color while reading along.
Features:12 bold and easy coloring pages perfect for ages 4–8
Large fill areas and thick outlines
Perforation marks so finished pages can be cut out and displayed
Single-sided pages recommended (blank backs included)
Encourages creativity, storytelling, and screen-free fun
A complete adventure from start to finish that kids will love coloring again and again.

authorSite.blurb: Join brave little T-Rex Rexy and his best friends Tri and Pip on an exciting quest to find the missing glowing egg!

books.title: Tasneem's Glider
books.subtitle: How Persistence Found the Wind
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: When Tasneem looks up at the sky, she doesn't just see birds — she sees a problem to solve.
Determined to build her own glider, she launches into action. First try: too heavy. Second try: too fragile. Third try: the wrong shape entirely.
But Tasneem doesn't give up. Every crash teaches her something new about gravity, lift, and the power of a well-curved wing.
With her cat Yuki watching and her curious heart refusing to quit, Tasneem's fourth glider catches the wind — and so does her spirit.
A joyful story for young inventors and future engineers who know that every 'failed' try is really just a lesson in disguise.
• Teaches persistence and growth mindset
• Introduces basic concepts: gravity, lift, mass, and shape
• Perfect for ages 5–7, STEM classrooms, and bedtime
