Curiosity + Persistence = Wings

authorSite.blurb: How Persistence Found the Wind. A story about Tasneem, her glider, and the power of not giving up.

books.title: The Code of the Cosmic Compass
books.subtitle: An M1Z3 Adventure
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: M1Z3 has no memory of who built him — only a strange Quantum Evolution Core that learns a little more about the galaxy (and himself) with every spark. When a mysterious brass holocube reveals the lost location of the legendary Starlight Engine, M1Z3 and his hologram co-pilot, Pixel, must out-fly a squad of scrap-drones, out-think an ancient vault, and find the first of three missing Cosmic Compass fragments — before it's too late.
A colorful, big-hearted science fiction adventure about curiosity, friendship, and the courage to grow, Book One launches a ten-book journey across the galaxy.
Perfect for readers ages 8–12 who love robots, space adventure, and stories where being curious is a superpower.

authorSite.blurb: An M1Z3 Adventure. A cosmic journey of codes, compasses, and courage.

books.title: The Great Dino Journey
books.subtitle: Helping Friends to the Warm Lands
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: A group of friendly dinosaurs (with more realistic body proportions and details, but kind smiling faces and expressive eyes) help each other travel from cold snowy lands to warm tropical shores. Every page has short motivational dialogue about teamwork, perseverance, kindness, and courage.
Special feature: Every coloring page has a dashed border so kids can color and cut out the pictures.

authorSite.blurb: A group of friendly dinosaurs (with more realistic body proportions and details, but kind smiling faces and expressive eyes) help each other travel from cold snowy lands to warm tropical shores.

books.title: The Little Robo
books.subtitle: A Story About Being Small, Being Different, and Being Brave
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Robo is the smallest robot in the whole shining city. Every day he asks the tall robots if he can play, and every day they look down, down, down and say the same thing: "Sorry, little one. You're too small." Robo begins to wonder if being small means he will never belong.

Then, on the night of the great city festival, a low barrier swings shut across the square — and the tall robots are far too big to fit beneath it. On the other side, their children are all alone. The grown-up robots push and pull, but no one can get through… no one except a robot small enough to wiggle underneath.

The Little Robo is a warm, gently told picture book about inclusion, courage, and self-worth — a reminder for every child that being different is not a problem to fix, but a gift the world needs. Perfect for reading aloud at bedtime, in the classroom, or anywhere a child needs to hear that they matter exactly as they are.

authorSite.blurb: A gentle story about a small robot and the big feelings that come with growing and belonging.

books.title: The Secret of High Park
books.subtitle: A Toronto Mystery Duo Adventure
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: A brass key. A secret riddle. A race across Toronto.

When Aidan’s sneaker catches on a loose stone in High Park, he and his dad, Zach, uncover a mystery more than a century old — a brass key, a riddle that must be solved by noon, and a stranger in a green coat who wants the prize for himself.

From historic Colborne Lodge to the steam engines of Roundhouse Park and the old lighthouse on the Toronto Islands, the father-and-son Toronto Mystery Duo must follow the clues, outsmart a thief, and bring home a treasure the city forgot.

Told in bold, full-colour comic panels, this fast-moving mystery is perfect for young detectives ages 6 to 10 — and a great read-together adventure for parents and kids who love maps, riddles, and hidden history in real places.
Book 1 of the Toronto Mystery Duo. The next case has already landed in the Duo’s hands…

authorSite.blurb: A brass key.

books.title: The Spiderweb Mystery
books.subtitle: Curiosity is a Superpower
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: What makes a spiderweb sparkle after the rain?

When curious five-year-old Aidan races into the garden after a big storm, he discovers something magical — every spiderweb is covered in perfect, glittering water drops. Instead of just wondering, he decides to find out why.

Following the five steps of the Scientific Method — Ask, Observe, Hypothesize, Test, and Learn — Aidan runs his own backyard experiment. Some of his ideas turn out to be wrong. But real scientists don't give up. They try again.
With vibrant illustrations and simple language, this gentle story introduces young children to scientific thinking and shows them that curiosity is the most powerful superpower of all.
Perfect for ages 5–7, classroom read-alouds, and budding young scientists everywhere.
Ask • Observe • Try • Discover

authorSite.blurb: Curiosity is a Superpower. A gentle mystery that celebrates asking questions and looking closer.
